entities.summary:
Otto I of Olomouc, known as Otto the Fair, was a member of the Přemyslid dynasty and Prince of Olomouc in Moravia from 1061 until his death in 1087. This eventful prince played a significant role in the medieval politics of Moravia and the surrounding regions. He was a key figure in the medieval history of the region, known for his diplomatic skills and his efforts to maintain the independence of Moravia.

Otto I was born in 1020 and died on June 9, 1087. He was the son of Vratislaus II, the Duke of Bohemia, and his wife, Gertrude of Klettgau.

His reign was marked by several significant events, including the Battle of Mlada Boleslav in 1048, which was a major victory for the Moravian army against the Polish and German forces. He also played a key role in the establishment of the Archbishopric of Prague in 1048.

Otto I's legacy extends beyond his own lifetime, as he laid the foundations for the independence of Moravia and the development of its unique culture. His diplomatic skills and strategic alliances helped to maintain the region's autonomy and ensured its continued existence as a major power in the medieval world.

The legacy of Otto I of Olomouc can be seen in the many monuments and structures that still stand today, including the Olomouc Castle, which was built during his reign.
